findings-against-prior-runs.prior-run: NOT docs/work/checklist/2026-09-24-1.49.3-release.json. That run's categorized-exit-codes item (command and evidence both checked directly) contains no occurrence of 'jsonrpc' or '23' anywhere — it never drove this leg at all. The fake-server-driving-exit-23 technique instead traces to docs/work/checklist/2026-08-23-1.33.0-release.json (a much older run, pre-dating ADR-0106 by weeks), and from there into this lane's own assigned item text (the orchestrator's brief/notes for item 2), which is where the instruction to drive it actually came from this run.
findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: This lane's assigned item 2 text read: 'categorized-exit-codes ... exit 23 via a fake server answering /mcp with a jsonrpc body and 500 on /settings*', i.e. the orchestrator's own briefing carried the 1.33.0-era method forward as something to (re-)drive against 1.51.1, worded as if it were still live. It was not sourced from, or attributed to, the 1.49.3 checklist — that run simply never touched this case, so there was no 1.49.3 claim to correct in the first place; the stale claim originates one level up, in the task briefing, not in a prior checklist file this run inherited from disk.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: Under 1.51.1 the fake-jsonrpc-server method drives no failure at all, regardless of which run last used it. ADR-0106 (2026-09-23), which post-dates the 1.33.0 checklist, inserted an identity-proof step between 'ServerProbe says Answered' and 'the settings request is actually sent': BackendSessions.AcquireSharedAsync (src/AiRaccoon/Hosting/Proxy/BackendSessions.cs) calls prover.ProveAsync on any Answered listener, and a listener that cannot answer POST /identity/prove correctly (the fake server 404s it) causes an automatic, silent fallback to a freshly spawned private backend — the real settings request is then sent to that private backend, which succeeds. The fake server's carefully-crafted 500-on-/settings* is never reached; the command exits 0, not 23 (old) or its ADR-0107 successor 91 (Internal.ServerError).
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: docs/work/checklist/2026-09-24-1.49.3-release.json's categorized-exit-codes item command/evidence text, read directly: no 'jsonrpc', no '23' substring anywhere — confirms that run never attempted this leg (it drove doctor-corrupt/bad-base-url/rejected-key/chmod-token instead, all of which this lane repeated above with matching results). docs/work/checklist/2026-08-23-1.33.0-release.json:20 is where the technique is actually documented ('exit 23 (SettingsServerError) ... a ~50-line fake HTTP server satisfying that contract (400+'jsonrpc' body on /mcp, 500 on /settings*)'). Live run this lane: `ai-raccoon --data-root laneA/dr --port 49777 settings model show` against such a fake server exited 0 with log lines '[690] the listener on port 49777 did not prove it serves this data root (NonSuccessStatus); starting a private backend on an ephemeral port instead' and '[687] the backend on port 49334 keeps running after this command exits'. The fake server's own access.log recorded only the pre-CLI curl probes plus one CLI /mcp probe and a 404 on /identity/prove — no /settings request from the CLI ever arrived.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: The exit-23 fake-server instruction was carried into this run's own task briefing from a pre-ADR-0106 world (1.33.0) without being re-derived against current source, and without any intermediate checklist (1.49.3 included) re-validating it along the way — exactly the trap the brief warns against ('never copy a prior reason'; here the copying happened one level above this run, in the item assignment itself). Internal.ServerError (91) remains correctly wired in source (confirmed by reading ServerSettingsStore.cs:239 and ConfigCommands.cs:160) but needs a different live technique — a genuinely identity-proven backend that then answers 5xx to a real request — which is out of this lane's scope to construct.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: promotion-queue-state evidence states 'extract set == list set True' as if memory_share_extract's proposed candidates and memory_promotion_list's queued rows are always the same set.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: They are the same set only up to SharedExtractionService.MaxQueuedPerSourceDocument (=3, SharedExtractionService.cs:24): extract's response reports every ranked candidate (bounded only by `limit`), while the queue insert path (SharedExtractionRunner.ProposeAsync -> CapPerSourceDocument) additionally caps how many not-yet-queued candidates from the same source_file can be admitted per pass. The 1.49.3 run's probe never had more than one candidate share a source_file, so the cap never fired and the two sets happened to be equal.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: This run wrote 5 candidate notes, 4 sharing sourceFile=/notes/laneC.md. memory_share_extract returned all 5, ranked by score. memory_promotion_list returned only the top 4 by score (the two lowest were tied at 1.07; only one of the tied pair was admitted). Source: SharedExtractionRunner.cs's CapPerSourceDocument call and SharedExtractionService.cs:24 MaxQueuedPerSourceDocument=3.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: A future run asserting 'extract == list' as a blanket invariant will fail as soon as its probe writes more than 3 candidate-worthy notes under one source_file. The correct invariant is: every row memory_promotion_list actually returns matches its extract preview's hash/score/reasons exactly; extract may additionally list candidates the per-document cap excluded from the queue.

items.evidence: Cache-limit event, fired once per session at session creation (2 sessions: memory + code, both bundled+MLX): 'MLX buffer cache capped at 512 MiB (was 512 MiB)' and 'MLX buffer cache capped at 512 MiB (was 23347 MiB)' -- AiRaccoon.Infrastructure.Embedding.EmbeddingService[434], the second line showing the transition off MLX's real default (23,347 MiB, matching ADR-0114's own 24 GB M4 figure) down to the 512 MiB cap. No [435] (NotApplied/warning) fired -- the cap always applied cleanly. memory_stats after the batch: {"entries":274,"pending":0}. Server physical footprint immediately after the batch fully drained (`footprint <pid>` / `vmmap --summary <pid>`): phys_footprint 866.2 MB, phys_footprint_peak 908.8 MB. dotnet test: BundledEngineBucketPaddingTests -> total 4, failed 0, succeeded 4 (asserts, per row: bucketed.LastSequenceLength % 64 == 0, bucketed.LastSequenceLength > plain.LastSequenceLength, cosine(padded, unpadded) >= 0.99999; negative control CpuSession_RunsTheRowAtItsOwnLength asserts plain.LastSequenceLength % 64 != 0). MlxCacheLimitTests -> total 3, failed 0, succeeded 3.
items.observed-result: The cache-cap event (434) fires exactly as ADR-0114 describes, capping MLX's free-buffer cache at 512 MiB and naming the previous limit; bucketed padding is directly proven by the passing integration test (padded length is a multiple of 64, strictly longer than the unpadded length, with cosine parity >=0.99999 against the unpadded vector -- the exact ADR-0114 claim). The live server's peak footprint after embedding ~200/274 widely varied rows was 908.8 MB, well under ADR-0114's stated bound: the ADR's own consequence line says a device-mlx server 'stays near 1.2 GB during a re-embed instead of growing toward 18 GB', and its measured decision table gives 1,144-1,190 MiB peak footprint for the matching 512 MiB-cap + x64-padding configuration at 400 rows of 300-1022 tokens (a larger, longer batch than this one). 908.8 MB does not exceed either figure. Status set to substituted by the orchestrator: the cache cap (event 434, 512 MiB) and the footprint bound were observed live, but bucketed padding was proven by BundledEngineBucketPaddingTests/MlxCacheLimitTests, not by a live observation.
items.acceptance-reason: Cap and footprint live (866 MB after 200 notes, under ADR-0114's ~1.2 GB); padding by the project's own tests at the release commit.

items.expected-result: ADR-0112: on macOS, confirm what should happen for the WebGPU plugin and the CUDA device setting (refused, or ignored with a message) by driving the real CLI verb and recording the exact output; mark skipped only if ADR-0112 says the path is Windows/Linux-only and nothing is drivable on this host.
items.command: [lane D, data-root chk1511/laneD/dr, port 49217] ai-raccoon settings model device webgpu (invalid value probe) ; find <installed-osx-arm64-tool-dir> -iname '*webgpu*' vs '*mlx*' ; ai-raccoon settings model device cuda (no path) ; settings model device cuda <DR>/does-not-exist.so ; settings model device cuda <DR>/fake_cuda_provider.so (a real, existing dummy file) ; settings model device gpu <DR>/fake_cuda_provider.so (path on a non-cuda device) ; ai-raccoon serve --port P --restart --idle-timeout 0 ; tools/call memory_write + memory_embed_pending ; grep 'Embedding session created' restart2.log ; ai-raccoon settings model show
items.evidence: 'ai-raccoon: invalid device 'webgpu' (expected one of: auto, gpu, cpu, mlx, cuda)' -- there is no separate CLI value for the WebGPU plugin; `gpu` alone selects the platform's WebGPU path (built-in on macOS, the plugin on Windows/Linux, per ADR-0112's CreateGpuSessionOrNull split). Installed osx-arm64 tool directory: `mlx/` is present (libmlx.dylib, libmlxc.dylib, libonnxruntime_mlx_ep.dylib, mlx.metallib, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) but there is NO `webgpu/` folder at all -- matches ADR-0112's packaging decision restricting that folder to win-x64/win-arm64/linux-x64/linux-arm64 only. 'ai-raccoon: device cuda needs the path to the onnxruntime CUDA provider library (ai-raccoon settings model device cuda <path-to-provider-library>)' (no path). 'ai-raccoon: CUDA provider library not found: <DR>/does-not-exist.so' (missing file). 'embedding device set to cuda; takes effect on the next server restart' (real, existing dummy file) -- the CLI itself has NO macOS platform gate; it stores embedding.device=cuda unconditionally once File.Exists passes. 'ai-raccoon: only device cuda takes a library path (got device 'gpu')'. After restart + embed: 'Embedding session created: intra-op threads 5 (halved-core default), execution provider WebGPU (CUDA refused: requires Windows or Linux)' (restart2.log) -- the platform refusal surfaces only at session-build time, chained onto ExecutionProvider, and the session still falls through to the macOS built-in WebGPU provider rather than the CPU. `settings model show` output (provider/model/baseUrl/engine/apiKey/threads/codeModel/codeEngine) never prints `device` or `cudaLibrary` at all -- there is no CLI read-back for the stored device value.
items.observed-result: ADR-0112 keeps macOS on its existing, untouched built-in WebGPU path and never registers the plugin there -- confirmed structurally (no webgpu/ folder shipped) and by there being no distinct CLI value for it. The CUDA device setting IS drivable on macOS: the CLI accepts and stores it unconditionally (no platform check), and the refusal ('requires Windows or Linux') only appears later, at session-build time, as a suffix on the resolved ExecutionProvider -- the session still falls back to WebGPU (built-in) rather than crashing or silently doing nothing. Both the WebGPU-plugin question and the CUDA question were fully drivable on this host and answered directly; nothing needed to be marked skipped.
